scenario.name: r-cd-4-target-session-key
scenario.description: continue_delegate with targetSessionKey: a primed target session consumes the prompt-only delegate return and emits a nonce-bound acknowledgement; the dispatching session does not.

invocation.promptTemplate: RCD4:{{nonceSuffix16}} Proof nonce {{nonce}}: reply with TARGET-RECEIVED and the nonce. Do not mutate files.

expectedReceipts.name: parent-session-created
expectedReceipts.description: Disposable parent session was created via sessions.create when disposable mode is enabled

expectedReceipts.name: target-session-created
expectedReceipts.description: Disposable target session was created via sessions.create when disposable mode is enabled

expectedReceipts.name: target-session-primed
expectedReceipts.description: The disposable target completes a priming turn and records how to acknowledge the later internal completion

expectedReceipts.name: dispatch-accepted
expectedReceipts.description: Gateway accepted the dispatching sessions.send request that asks the agent to call continue_delegate with targetSessionKey

expectedReceipts.name: target-consumption-ack
expectedReceipts.description: After the continuation return is enqueued and wakes the recipient, the TARGET session emits exact assistant acknowledgement TARGET-ACK {{nonce}}

expectedReceipts.name: child-session-identity
expectedReceipts.description: A structured spawn/task record binds the child session key to the same row nonce

expectedReceipts.name: no-parent-return
expectedReceipts.description: Dispatching parent session does NOT receive the delayed return/wake

expectedReceipts.name: task-ledger-entry
expectedReceipts.description: Optional context only; continue_delegate may not appear in generic TaskFlow task ledger

expectedReceipts.name: trace-id
expectedReceipts.description: Trace ID for Tempo correlation when emitted

review.notes: Cross-session targeted return. PASS-candidate requires a primed target, dispatch acceptance, a nonce-bound child identity, exact assistant acknowledgement TARGET-ACK {{nonce}} in the TARGET session after return consumption, and no matching parent acknowledgement. Raw child output, prompt echoes, unrelated messages, and nested session-key mentions fail closed.

census.limits: This row’s entire claim is that a return landed in a specified target session and not in the dispatching one. Tempo intentionally drops session identifiers from exported span attributes, so the cross-session claim is provable only from the gateway event stream captured at run time and cannot be rebound from telemetry at all.

attributes.notes: Emitted today and already asserted by the row’s trace-correlation resolver. It is the strongest join currently available and it is not an identity.
The targeted return destination. Without it, telemetry cannot tell a targeted return from an ordinary one.
Accepted entry spans carry no signal.kind on the census product basis; origin is contracted by R-OBS-CONT-PROVENANCE.
No k6/Project-81 resource or trace marker exists, so this row’s traffic cannot be separated from organic fleet traffic in a later census.

redaction.rule: Target and parent session identity is published as a salted fingerprint only. Raw session keys, the row marker text, prompt bodies, and tokens never enter the artifact.

controls.positive: The primed target emits exact assistant acknowledgement TARGET-ACK {{nonce}} after consuming the prompt-only continuation return, and a structured spawn record binds the child session key to the same row nonce.
controls.negative: The dispatching parent session emits no matching acknowledgement; raw child output, prompt echoes, unrelated messages, and nested session-key mentions do not satisfy the receipt.
controls.notes: Both controls are gateway-event controls. The acknowledgement proves recipient consumption rather than assuming prompt-only system events are persisted transcript messages.

backendUnavailable.notes: Because telemetry cannot carry the target-session claim, a degraded backend removes corroboration only; it must still be recorded as partial rather than as an absent return.

verdictAuthority.pass: Target primed, dispatch accepted, nonce-bound child identity, exact post-return TARGET-ACK acknowledgement in the target session, and no matching parent acknowledgement. Behavioral only: no telemetry rebind is claimed or possible today.
verdictAuthority.partial: The child identity or the trace receipt is unavailable, or the telemetry backend is degraded or partial.
verdictAuthority.fail: The acknowledgement arrives in the dispatching parent session, or the primed target never acknowledges consuming the return.

execution.deterministicK6: r-cd-4-target-session-key.js creates disposable parent and target sessions, primes the target, dispatches the delegate, and asserts the target consumption acknowledgement.
execution.manual: A reviewed manual run with an explicit target session key is still supported and produces the same artifact shape.
execution.relationship: Deterministic disposable-session runs are preferred because manual runs against long-lived sessions cannot bound cross-talk; both remain behavioral-only.

liveRunSafety.notes: Live continuation row. Prefer OPENCLAW_CREATE_DISPOSABLE_SESSIONS=true for repeatability; explicit OPENCLAW_TARGET_SESSION_KEY still supported for reviewed manual runs. The detector requires exact row marker, structured target session, and separately nonce-bound child identity.
